# 不退轉法輪經

**ID:** T0267
**Volume:** T09
**Category:** 法華部類
**Original Category:** 法華部
**Byline:** 失譯
**Juans:** 4
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T0267

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A four-*juan* anonymous early Chinese translation of the *Avaivartika-cakra-sūtra* — the second of the three Chinese translations of the same Indic source-text preserved in the canon. The Taishō cross-reference 「No. 267 [Nos. 266, 268]」 documents the parallel translations: T266 = Dharmarakṣa's *Fóshuō Āwéiyuèzhì zhē jīng* ([KR6d0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0105)), T267 = the present anonymous translation, T268 = Zhìyán's *Fóshuō Guǎngbó yánjìng bùtuìzhuǎn lún jīng* ([KR6d0107](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0107)).

**Abstract**

The *Bùtuìzhuǎn fǎlún jīng* is the second of the three Chinese translations of the Indic *Avaivartika-cakra-sūtra*. Its anonymous Liáng-period attribution places it in the early-fifth-century Northern Liáng productive context, when the Liáng courts at Liángzhōu sponsored substantial Buddhist translation activity that supplemented and frequently competed with the contemporary Cháng'ān translation bureau under Kumārajīva.

The work's four-*juan* extent (against Dharmarakṣa's three-*juan* in [KR6d0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6d/KR6d0105)) suggests either a different recension of the Indic text or substantial expansion in translation. Comparison of the three Chinese translations against the Tibetan and any surviving Indic fragments would clarify the textual relationships, but no detailed comparative study has been published.

The dating is bracketed within the Northern Liáng productive period (397–439).
